slides.text:
In Go the condition of an `if` has no parentheses, and the braces are never optional. `else if` and `else` start on the same line as the closing brace: a new line before `else` is a syntax error.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
Go has no `?:` operator. To pick a value, declare the variable first and set it inside the branches.

An `if` can start with a short statement and a `;`. The variable it declares is visible in every branch of the chain, and nowhere after it.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.

exercises.title: Choose with if
exercises.guide: Pick one branch out of a chain of conditions.

chunks.guide: No parentheses around the conditions, and the braces are required. The first true branch runs, and `else` catches the rest.

notes.text: else stays on the line of the closing brace.

chunks.guide: This line runs after the chain.

exercises.title: Why is it rejected?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the cause.
options: The condition must be a `bool`, not an `int`
`stock` has to be a constant in a condition
exercises.explanation: Go never turns a number into true or false. The condition must already be a `bool`, so write `stock > 0`.

exercises.title: Pick a value with if
exercises.guide: There is no `?:` in Go: declare a variable, then set it in each branch.

chunks.guide: Declare `advice` before the `if`, so both branches can set it. After the block it still holds the value.

notes.text: Declared outside, so both branches can reach it.
A plain = sets it. A := would make a new one.

exercises.title: Declare inside the if
exercises.guide: Declare a variable in the `if` line and test it.

chunks.guide: A price to charge a fee on.
The statement before the `;` runs first, then the condition decides. `fee` is visible in both branches and gone after the closing brace.

notes.text: Runs first. fee exists only for this if.
After the semicolon comes the real condition.
The else branch still sees fee.

chunks.guide: This line runs after the chain.

exercises.title: Use the setup variable
exercises.guide: Declare a variable in the setup of the `if`, then print that same variable in the `else` branch.

exercises.title: Split and test in one line
exercises.guide: Split an email at the `@` and use the found flag as the condition.

chunks.guide: An address to split. The imports are already in the file.
`strings.Cut` returns three values: the text before the separator, the text after it, and a `bool` that says if it was found.

notes.text: Gives before, after and a found flag.
A bool already, so it works alone as the condition.
